title: Broadstone Hall Primary School: 14 July 2026
text:
Determination
Case reference: VAR2760
Admission Authority: Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council for
Broadstone Hall Primary School
Date of decision: 14 July 2026
Determination
In accordance with section 88E of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998, I
approve the proposed variation to the admission arrangements determined by
Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council for Broadstone Hall Primary School for
2027/28.
I determine that for admission in 2027/28 the published admission number will be 60.
The referral
1. Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council is the admission authority for Broadstone
Hall Primary School (the School) and has referred to the adjudicator a proposal for a
variation to the admission arrangements for the School for 2027/28 (the arrangements).
2. The School is a community school for children aged three to eleven years. Stockport
Metropolitan Borough Council is also the local authority for the area in which the School is
located and I shall refer to it as the local authority. The School is in an urban area with eight
other schools which admit children to reception year within one mile and around 90 within
three miles.
3. The proposed variation is that the published admission number (PAN) for the School
is reduced from 75 to 60 for admissions in 2027/28; a reduction of 15 places. The year of
entry is reception year and this is the year group to which the PAN applies.
Jurisdiction and procedure
4. Section 88E of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998 (the Act) makes
provision for variations to determined arrangements. Paragraphs 3.6 and 3.7 of the School
Admissions Code (the Code) say (insofar as is relevant here):

“3.6 Once admission arrangements have been determined for a particular school year,
they cannot be revised by the admission authority unless such revision is necessary to
give effect to a mandatory requirement of this Code, admissions law, a determination
of the Adjudicator or any misprint in the admission arrangements. Admission
authorities may propose other variations where they consider such changes to be
necessary in view of a major change in circumstances. Such proposals must be
referred to the Schools Adjudicator for approval, and the appropriate bodies notified.
Where the local authority is the admission authority for a community or voluntary
controlled school, it must consult the governing body of the school before making any
reference.
3.7 Admission authorities must notify the appropriate bodies of all variations”.
5. The arrangements were determined by the local authority on 10 February 2026. The
local authority has provided me with confirmation that the appropriate bodies have been
notified of the proposed variation in line with the Code and confirmation that the governing
body of the School has been consulted on the proposed variation and supports it.
6. I find that the appropriate procedures were followed, and I am satisfied that the
proposed variation is within my jurisdiction.
7. In the interest of dealing speedily with this and other cases, I have not considered
other aspects of the arrangements. Therefore, nothing in this determination should be taken
as indicating that other aspects of the arrangements do or do not conform with the
requirements relating to admissions.
8. In considering the variation request, I have had regard to all relevant legislation and
the Code.
9. The information I have considered in reaching my decision includes:
a) the referral from the local authority dated 16 June 2026;
b) the determined arrangements for 2027/28 and the proposed variation to those
arrangements;
c) responses from the School to my requests for further information;
d) maps showing the location of the School; and
e) information available on government websites including:
o ‘Get Information About Schools’ (GIAS);
o Ofsted;
o ‘Financial Benchmarking and Insights Tool’ (FBIT); and
o ‘Find and compare schools and colleges in England’ (the DfE website);
f) the websites for the local authority and the School.
2

10. There is no formal consultation required for a variation and so parents and others do
not have the opportunity to express their views. Clearly it is desirable that changes to
arrangements are made via the process of determination following consultation as the
consultation process allows those with an interest to express their views. It also allows for
objections to the adjudicator. None of this is afforded by the variation process.
11. The arrangements for 2028/29 have not yet been determined. This means that if I
decide to approve the proposed variation to the arrangements for 2027/28 as proposed, it
will have the effect of forming the ‘baseline’ for subsequent years. I note that the local
authority intends to consult on setting the PAN at 60 for 2028/29.
Consideration of proposed variation
12. Paragraph 3.6 of the Code (as above) requires that admission arrangements, once
determined, may only be revised, that is changed or varied, if there is a major change of
circumstance or certain other limited and specified circumstances. I will consider below
whether the proposed variation is justified by the change in circumstances.
13. The local authority told me that the reason for it seeking a variation for the School is
that the number of children needing a place in reception year is falling across the area and
at the School. Schools are funded largely by the number of pupils and the greatest cost is
staffing. This means that if a School has a number of small classes, it is unlikely to receive
sufficient funding to meet the costs. Most primary schools seek to have close to 30 pupils to
a class in order to be financially efficient.
14. The School is one subject to the School Admissions (Infant Class Sizes) (England)
Regulations 2012 (the Infant Class Size Regulations) which require that infant classes
(those where the majority of children will reach the age of five, six or seven during the
school year) must not contain more than 30 pupils with a single qualified school teacher
except in specific exceptional circumstances. The Infant Class Size Regulations apply to
reception year, year 1 and year 2.
15. The local authority and the School are concerned that the combination of falling
demand for the School and the requirements of the Infant Class Size Regulations means
that the School will accrue a financial deficit if the PAN is not reduced. I will first consider
the applications and admissions overall including whether there would be sufficient school
places in the area if I were to agree the variation. I will then consider demand for places at
the School and the reasons for the variation request.
16. The local authority has a duty to ensure that there are sufficient school places for the
children in its area. To fulfil this duty the local authority assesses the likely future number of
places to be needed and plans to meet that need. The local authority uses planning areas,
which are geographical areas and the schools within those areas, for this purpose. The
School is in a planning area of eight schools, including the School, which admit children to
reception year.
3

17. Parents can apply for admission for their children wherever they wish and will make
their decisions based on their circumstances and will consider factors such as convenience,
family connections and reputation. Parents will take no account of planning areas when
applying for a school place.

18. When applying for a school place, parents in the local authority’s area are able to
express up to six preferences. A first preference is the school to which a parent would most
like their child to be admitted. Table 1 shows that demand has reduced in the planning area
from 400 children offered places for 2024/25 to 347 offered places for 2026/27. The number
of vacant places based on offers in 2026 is 88, which is over 20 per cent or one fifth of the
total number of places available. This is a very high proportion. There is a higher number of
vacant places forecast for 2027 and I am assured that if the PAN were reduced to 60 that
there would be sufficient places to meet demand for 2027/28. The number of vacancies
forecast for 2028/29 is similar to 2027/28 so I am not concerned that setting the baseline
would lead to a lack of places for 2028/29.
19. I will now consider demand for the School, parental preference and the reasons for
requesting the reduction in PAN in more detail. Table 2 shows demand for the School and
forecast demand.

20. I note that the local authority said,
“it is important to consider the nuances of parental preference and the actual number
of children offered places in previous years. For the September 2026 intake, the
forecast was 65, yet only 63 pupils were offered places on National Offer Day and
this has since dropped to 62 pupils. Similarly, for the 2025 intake, the forecast was
73, and 70 pupils started on the first day of the academic year.”
21. FBIT recorded that at the end of the financial year April 2024 to March 2025, the in-
year balance was £64,247 and the reserves were £97,325. I asked the School to provide
further information about its finances and the planned class organisation taking into account
whether I agreed the variation or not.
22. The School told me that for the end of the 2025 – 2026 financial year, the in-year
balance was £56,453 and the revenue reserve was £153,778. Therefore the financial
situation for the School improved in the last financial year. However, the School forecasts
for 2027 – 2028, the School would have a revenue reserve deficit of £139,466 if the
variation is not agreed. Clearly all forecast figures are subject to a variety of factors but give
an indication of possible outcomes. I note that once a school is in a financial deficit, it is
hard to address without implications for teaching and learning at a school as every budget
line must be affected, particularly staffing and resources.
23. In terms of class organisation, the School currently provides 19 classes, with three
for the current reception year of around 22 and 23 pupils each. Other year groups have
some mixed aged classes, as one would expect from a school with a PAN of 75, and some
single year group classes. I note that year 6 has three single year group classes with 20, 22
and 23 pupils. A similar pattern is planned for the 2026/27 academic year for year 6.
24. The School plans 16 classes for the 2026/27 academic year with two classes of 30
for reception year, even though 63 children have accepted places. Sixteen classes are
partly achieved by classes of over 30 pupils in years 3 and 4, which are not infant classes,
and 60 children or fewer in reception year. The School wishes to work towards two classes
to each year group.
25. I note that the local authority forecasts that 68 parents will put the School as their first
preference for 2027/28. Forecasts of the number of children for reception year are
challenging as the children concerned are not in school and forecasts of parental
preference will be largely based on the number of births, the number of children in pre-
5

school provision and previous patterns. It is particularly difficult to forecast demand for
specific primary schools.
26. In considering this matter I have balanced the possible frustration of parental
preference against the likely impact on the School’s financial and educational health of the
PAN remaining at 75. It is probable that if the PAN is 60 in 2027, then a number of parents
may not be able to achieve their first preference. It is clear, however, that there are a high
number of schools within a short distance of the School and so a high chance of admission
to a local school. I note that if the variation is made now, parents will be able to apply in the
knowledge of the PAN set.
27. The number of children seeking a place at the School has fallen, in line with
demographic trends, and the School seeks a pragmatic approach to responding to this with
a PAN which allows it to remain a financially healthy educational establishment. Taking
these matters into account, I approve the reduction in PAN from 75 to 60 for admissions in
2027/28.
28. I also ask the local authority to note that it could request a reduction to the PAN for
2026/27. I cannot say what the outcome of such a request would be and note that any child
for whom a place has been offered would have to be admitted. However, if the PAN were to
be set at 60 and pupil numbers were to reduce to that level, the local authority would not
have to admit over 60 in 2026/27, although it would remain open to any parent refused a
place to appeal.
Determination
29. In accordance with section 88E of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998, I
approve the proposed variation to the admission arrangements determined by Stockport
Metropolitan Borough Council for Broadstone Hall Primary School for 2027/28.
30. I determine that for admission in 2027/28 the published admission number will be 60.
Dated: 14 July 2026
Signed:
Schools Adjudicator: Deborah Pritchard
